Subject: Post-demo recap + next steps (p95/p99 latency qualification)

Alex / Priya  thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the SLO qualification for end-to-end latency (hosted Redwood API vs your current provider):

Summary of requirements we captured on the call:
- Primary SLOs: p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 900ms end-to-end for single-shot text generation (avg request size ~150 tokens).
- Concurrency: sustained 120 concurrent active sessions during peak; short bursts up to 500 concurrent.
- Throughput: average 8 reqs/sec across sustained window, peak ~20 reqs/sec during bursts.
- Streaming: client requires streaming token-by-token for low-latency UX (must start delivering tokens within 50ms of first token generation).
- Failure / fallback behavior: if hosted node fails, auto-fallback to a slightly higher-latency variant is acceptable provided no more than 1% request loss.

Proposed validation plan (we can share a test harness):
1) Exchange short-lived eval keys for a dedicated hosted-test route.
2) Run two staged tests: (A) baseline  replay 10k production requests (recorded traces) against your current provider; (B) Redwood hosted  same replay + streaming checks.
3) Collect p50/p95/p99, tail latencies, token-start times for streaming, and error/retry rates.
4) Review results together and map any regression causes (network vs model vs runtime).

Ask from you today: can you share a representative sample of request traces + current provider p95/p99 numbers? Also confirm whether we should include longer-generation (5001k token) tails in the same run or as a follow-up.

I attached a short SLO test plan (slo_test_plan_redwood.pdf)  it outlines the harness and metrics we'll collect. If that looks good, we'll schedule a 1-hr validation window. Proposed slots: Thu 07/02 10:0011:00 PDT or Fri 07/03 09:0010:00 PDT.

Thanks  happy to adjust.


Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa  great summary and appreciated the clear next steps. Quick answers and I've attached our most recent run (finlytics_current_provider_metrics.csv).

Answers:
- Current provider (vendor X) reported end-to-end historically: p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1.1s (for your 150-token avg). We see p99 spikes during heavy concurrency.
- Concurrency: our baseline production concurrency is around 100130 sustained, with occasional peaks to ~480 for brief ~12 minute bursts.
- Throughput: matches what you listed  ~79 rps sustained, peaks ~1822 rps.
- Streaming: currently the provider uses a chunked stream; token-start times are often 150250ms depending on network and model warm state.

We are happy to run the recorded-trace replay. We'll include two trace buckets: normal (avg 150 tokens) and long-tail (600800 tokens)  please advise if Redwood wants both in the same session.

Proposed test window: Thu 07/02 10:00 PDT works for us. We will share the traces and a small set of anonymized logs (no PII) by EOD today.

Alex / Priya  thanks for the metrics. A few technical clarifications from our side to make the test results comparable:

1) Network path: please confirm the client origin (region) and whether you want us to run the hosted eval from us-west-2 or us-east-1 to match production.
2) Warm vs cold model instances: our test harness can simulate cold starts by clearing KV cache between runs; please indicate if your historical numbers include cold starts.
3) Streaming measurement: we'll report two metrics  token-start latency (time until first token chunk leaves server) and token-arrival steady-state (inter-token latency). Token-start target: <=50ms for first chunk under normal warm conditions; we'll flag network-dominant latencies separately.
4) Concurrency profile: we'll run sustained 120 concurrent and a separate burst test to 500 concurrency for 5min. That will capture queueing/backpressure behavior.

Proposed acceptance criteria (preliminary):
- p95 <= 300ms for average-length requests
- p99 <= 900ms or documented root cause / mitigation plan if higher
- token-start <= 50ms for streaming under warm conditions for >=95% of requests

Logistics we need from Finlytics before Thu 07/02 10:00 PDT:
- 1) representative request traces (.jsonl)  thanks for committing to share these
- 2) short-lived test API key or allowlist IPs for our test route
- 3) preferred test region (us-west-2 or us-east-1)

If you prefer, we can run an initial low-risk smoke test before the full 1-hr window to verify connectivity and key/allowlist.


